name: Prompt engine
author: Brett
description: A general prompting / rules engine with its own control panel (prompt-engine@1, framework/core/engines/prompt-engine.mjs). Prompt events: a trigger (any console, axHub or build event: a build failed, something went to UI Review, a held call, a merge clash, a watchdog alert, a schedule, a spoken phrase, a webhook, a custom event), conditions (AND / OR groups over the event's fields, thresholds), limits (cooldown, dedupe, per hour), and what to ask Brett (approve / deny, a veto countdown, pick from options, text; as a dialog, a push, email, SMS or a phone call through axHub connectors, shown as keys needed until a connector exists). Every answer runs actions: tools (any plugin command through control@1), console commands, macros (saved sequences with parameters), pipelines (stages with gates Brett answers in between), orchestrator builds, notifications, or another event (chained rules). Every plugin registers its events, actions and connectors with a prompt-manifest@1 (plugin.json promptManifest) and the builder only offers what is valid for what is already picked. Templates for the common rules, test-fire (dry run shows the prompt and the plan per answer), history and an audit log. The control panel (Builds → Prompt engine) lists, creates, edits, switches, test-fires and answers; the same reaches REST, MCP, the CLI and voice through plugin-commands@1.

items.title: Prompt engine state
items.description: Every rule (with a one-line summary), macro, pipeline and waiting prompt, the counts and the registry summary (voice: 'what prompt rules do I have', 'anything waiting for me').

items.title: List rules
items.description: Every prompt event rule with its summary (voice: 'list my prompt rules').

items.title: One rule
items.description: A rule in full: trigger, conditions, limits, what it asks and what runs on each answer.

items.title: Add a rule
items.description: Create a prompt event rule (prompt-event@1): { id?, title, trigger: { source, event, filter? }, when?, limits?, ask: { kind, title, text?, options?, countdownSec?, outputs? }, on: { approve|deny|timeout|later|text|fire: [actions], pick: { option: [actions] } } }. Refused with the field named when it is not valid (voice: 'make a rule: when a build fails ask me to retry or archive it').

items.title: Change a rule
items.description: Change any part of a rule (the fields given replace those parts; the id stays).

items.title: Turn a rule on
items.description: Enable a rule (voice: 'turn on the build failed rule').

items.title: Turn a rule off
items.description: Disable a rule; it stays and can be turned on again (voice: 'turn off the UI review popup rule').

items.title: Delete a rule
items.description: Remove a rule for good; confirm = the rule id.

items.title: Test-fire a rule
items.description: Fire a rule with a sample event (or the event given), limits ignored. Dry by default: shows whether it fires, the prompt it would ask and the plan for every answer, runs nothing. live = true really asks / runs (voice: 'test the build failed rule').

items.title: List macros
items.description: Every macro (a saved sequence of actions with parameters).

items.title: Add a macro
items.description: Create a macro (prompt-macro@1): { id?, title, params?: [{ name, type?, default?, required? }], steps: [{ action, input }] }.

items.title: List pipelines
items.description: Every pipeline (ordered stages of actions; a stage may carry a gate Brett answers before it goes on).

items.title: Add a pipeline
items.description: Create a pipeline (prompt-pipeline@1): { id?, title, params?, stages: [{ id?, title, actions: [...], gate?: { kind, title, ... } }] }.

items.title: The registry
items.description: Every source with its events (and their fields), actions (and their inputs) and connectors: the built-in ones plus what every plugin registered (voice: 'what events can a rule fire on').

items.title: Register a manifest
items.description: A plugin, app, tool or service registers its events, actions and connectors (prompt-manifest@1). The same source again replaces the earlier one.

items.title: Builder choices
items.description: Context-aware choices for the builder: given what is picked so far ({ source?, event?, field?, ask?, action?, input? }) the valid sources, events, fields, operators, values, answers, actions and action inputs, with live lists (builds, plugins and their commands, macros, pipelines, rules).

items.title: Rule templates
items.description: Ready-made rules for the common cases (UI Review pop-up, build failed, held call veto, merge clash, model upgrade, watchdog, service down, daily digest, build shipped).

items.title: Add a rule from a template
items.description: Create a rule from a template, optionally with its own id / title (voice: 'add the build failed template').

items.title: Prompts waiting for Brett
items.description: Every prompt waiting for an answer (and the shelved ones), numbered, with the options to pick from (voice: 'what is waiting for me').

items.title: Answer a prompt
items.description: Answer a waiting prompt by id or number: approve, deny, later, pick (option id, number or label) or text. The rule's actions for that answer run at once (voice: 'approve it', 'pick option 2', 'deny the first one').

instance.description: prompt id, or its number in the waiting list

items.title: Fire an event
items.description: Send any event through the engine ({ source, event, payload }); every matching rule asks or runs. dry = true evaluates and plans only (voice: 'fire a custom event called deploy done').

items.title: Webhook in
items.description: An incoming webhook: fires webhook.received with { hook, headers, body } for rules to match.

items.title: Run the tick now
items.description: Expire prompts past their deadline (a veto runs, a pick takes its default) and fire the schedules that are due. The server runs this every minute by itself.

items.title: History
items.description: The audit log newest first: fired, skipped (and why), asked, answered, expired, planned, ran, failed, dry runs, keys needed; filter by rule, instance or kind (voice: 'show the prompt engine history').
